title: feat: portals — expose agent-run dev servers to the operator

commit.messageHeadline: feat(protocol): add portal methods and event
feat(gateway): add portal service and reverse proxy
feat(agents): add portal tool
fix(gateway): refine portal URL and proxy auth
refactor(gateway): keep portal helper types private
fix(gateway): declare portal transport service
test(gateway): satisfy portal proxy lint
test(gateway): narrow websocket payload types
refactor(protocol): compact portal schema exports
fix(gateway): export portal protocol types
feat(ui): add portals page
docs(gateway): add portals guide
fix(gateway): dial portal targets via localhost dual-stack
fix(gateway): type portal dual-stack connection
fix: satisfy portal integration gates
fix(gateway): isolate portal cookie jars per target
fix(ui): detect unreachable portals behind proxied gateways
test(ui): satisfy portal reachability lint
test(gateway): provide control UI request hosts
chore(protocol): regenerate after rebase
fix(gateway): namespace portal auth cookies by listener
fix(gateway): scope portal token URLs to write-capable clients
docs(web): list the portals route
fix(gateway): type portal open credentials
docs(gateway): clarify portals PORT/PUBLIC_URL are agent-set
chore(protocol): regenerate portal models
style(gateway): format portal method-order assertions
chore(plugin-sdk): refresh API baseline after rebase
chore(plugin-sdk): refresh API baseline after rebase
chore(protocol): refresh portal event order after rebase
chore(plugin-sdk): refresh API baseline after rebase
fix(gateway): pin portal referrer policy to no-referrer

Both P1 findings are addressed as of 7f4dbc02ce3.

**Isolate Gateway cookies from portal targets** — the proxy now enforces per-target cookie jars by name prefixing: only cookies carrying this portal's own `oc_portal_<port>_` prefix are forwarded upstream (prefix stripped), so Gateway plugin-auth cookies and sibling portals' cookies can never reach an agent-run app. Every target `Set-Cookie` — including on the WebSocket 101 handshake, which is parsed with a bounded header window — is rewritten to the prefixed name with `Domain` dropped, so a target cannot set or shadow a Gateway-hostname cookie. Boundary regressions cover: gateway-ish cookie + portal cookie in → target sees no cookie header (HTTP and WS upgrade); target session cookie round-trips through the prefix; cross-portal prefixes are not forwarded.

**Route portal traffic through supported remote access** — the Portals page now probes the portal origin from the browser (`no-cors` fetch, 4s timeout; CSP `connect-src` widened only to the page's own hostname across ports) before rendering the iframe. When the portal port is not reachable — Tailscale Serve/Funnel or a reverse proxy exposing only the Gateway port — the page shows a recovery notice with the gateway-host URL and a retry button instead of a dead iframe. The docs limitation section matches. A routed transport through the Gateway origin is deliberately deferred to the planned remote-worker portals follow-up, where the same transport is needed anyway.

On the decision question: keeping per-port listeners with enforced cookie-jar isolation is the owner call here — the prefix boundary removes the cookie-leak class the contract in `control-ui-plugin-auth-cookie.ts` protects against, without giving up root-path proxying (which is what keeps unmodified dev servers working). The "stored data model" note is a false positive: portals hold no persistent state; `portals.test.ts` under the protocol schema directory is wire-schema validation, not a database schema.

nodes.body:
Addressed the referrer finding in 54cead433c0 — good catch, this was a real leak path.

The portal URL carries its bearer token in the query and upstream response headers are copied verbatim, so a target answering with `Referrer-Policy: unsafe-url` could hand that URL to every third-party origin it references. The proxy now **overwrites** `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` after the upstream header copy (on proxied responses and on the 401/502 pages), rather than merely defaulting it, and additionally drops any inbound `Referer` that still carries the token before forwarding upstream — on both the HTTP and WebSocket-upgrade paths — so the credential cannot reach the target that way either.

The regression fails on pre-fix code for the intended reason (`expected 'unsafe-url' to be 'no-referrer'`) and passes after.
